senses.text: any of numerous small gallinaceous birds: such as
an Old World migratory game bird (Coturnix coturnix)

entries.history: Middle English quaile, from Anglo-French, from Medieval Latin quaccula, of imitative origin

phrases.meaning: any of a family (Turnicidae) of small terrestrial Old World birds that resemble quails and have only three toes on a foot with the hind toe being absent
a quail (Coturnix japonica synonym C. coturnix japonica) of eastern Asia that is sometimes raised for its meat or eggs and is used in laboratory research

senses.text: to recoil in dread or terror cower

synonyms.title: synonyms
synonyms.text: recoil shrink flinch wince blench quail mean to draw back in fear or distaste. recoil implies a start or movement away through shock, fear, or disgust. shrink suggests an instinctive recoil through sensitiveness, scrupulousness, or cowardice. flinch implies a failure to endure pain or face something dangerous or frightening with resolution. wince suggests a slight involuntary physical reaction (such as a start or recoiling). blench implies fainthearted flinching. quail suggests shrinking and cowering in fear.

senses.text: an unsweetened custard pie usually having a savory filling (such as spinach, mushrooms, or ham)

phrases.meaning: a quiche containing cheese and bacon bits

senses.text: expressive of puzzlement, curiosity, or disbelief
